_comment: Field selection for the gnomAD exome/genome callsets (VEP parquet).
INCLUDE-list: 'load': true is what reaches the parquet.
Generated from the v4.1.1 chr21 header; the 46 VEP subfields are
identical between exomes and genomes, verified on chr21.
One output row per (variant x transcript x consequence): the VEP
block is exploded, not stored as the packed string gnomAD ships.
Order used when a variant carries VEP in both callsets. Measured on
chr21: only 1.9% of variants are in both, and their VEP blocks are
byte-identical in 5781/5782 cases — the single exception differs
only in the order of terms inside Consequence, which disappears
once the block is exploded. So this is a deterministic tie-break,
not a content decision.

explode._comment: Split multi-term Consequence on '&', one row per term.

_comment: A pre-filter, not the real one. Applied per callset against that
callset's own AC, so this DTP stays independent of the joint
branch (ADR-003: the two data sources must not depend on each
other).
3, not 5: a variant can only reach a combined AC of 5 if one
callset has at least 3, since AC_joint is exactly AC_exomes +
AC_genomes. So 3 keeps everything the bundle will want, while 5
silently dropped the variants that clear the combined bar without
either callset reaching it — 45,974 of them on chr22, 1.6% of the
bundle's variants, left with no VEP annotation at all.
The real filter is the combined-AC pass after both VCFs are read,
which reduces variant_predictions to the variants whose summed AC
clears min_ac_combined and then semi-joins this table against it.
Setting this to null keeps every annotation gnomAD publishes, at
roughly 6.6x the intermediate size, with no effect on the final
table.
Side output: chromosome/position/ref/alt -> rsID, written as its
own table rather than stamped onto variant_masters.
The joint callset carries no rsID at all (its ID column is empty
on every record); only the exome and genome VCFs do, which is why
this is produced here.
IMPORTANT: rows are captured BEFORE the AC filter above. Measured
on chr21, only ~25% of rsIDs survive AC>=5, and the ones dropped
are the rare variants that most need an identifier.
min_ac tunes how much of the map is kept:
null -> every rsID gnomAD publishes (chr21: 9.85 M keys,
75 MB; extrapolates to ~4.5 GB genome-wide, about 30%
on top of the bundle). Can translate any gnomAD rsID,
including variants the bundle itself filtered out.
3    -> safe lower bound for the joint's AC>=5: a variant can
only reach a combined AC of 5 if one callset has at
least 3, since AC_joint is exactly AC_exomes +
AC_genomes (verified on 250,000 records). Loses no
variant the bundle keeps.
5    -> smallest map, but misses variants that clear the
combined threshold without either callset doing so.
Side output: the in-silico predictor scores gnomAD publishes as
INFO fields of the exome and genome sites VCFs — beside the CSQ
block this DTP was already reading, not inside it. Verified
against the header of gnomad.exomes.v4.1.1.sites.chr21.vcf.bgz:
415 INFO fields, of which these eight are the predictors, all
Number=1 Type=Float and therefore per site, not per transcript.
The joint callset does not carry them: its 664 INFO fields are
entirely frequency, count and QC, so no config change on the
joint DTP can recover them. 4.2.x read them from there.
A table of its own rather than columns on variant_masters, which
comes from the joint callset and does not carry these at all.
One row per variant allele: deduped across the two callsets, where
on chr22 all 901,714 variants present in both carry identical
scores, because a predictor is computed from the reference and the
allele, not by the callset.
The filter is the variant_master join above, not 'filters' below.
That one is a pre-filter that only bounds the intermediate.

fields.name: cadd_raw_score
fields.description: Raw CADD score; the extent to which the variant's annotation profile suggests deleteriousness.

fields.name: cadd_phred
fields.description: CADD Phred-like scaled C-score, 1 to 99, by rank against all possible substitutions.

fields.name: revel_max
fields.description: Maximum REVEL score at the site's MANE Select or canonical transcript; ensemble missense predictor.

fields.name: sift_max
fields.description: Scaled probability that the amino acid substitution is tolerated, 0 to 1.

fields.name: polyphen_max
fields.description: Predicted impact of the amino acid substitution on protein structure and function.

fields.name: spliceai_ds_max
fields.description: SpliceAI max delta score; probability the variant is splice-altering.

fields.name: pangolin_largest_ds
fields.description: Pangolin's largest delta score across two splicing consequences.

fields.name: phylop
fields.description: Base-wise conservation across the 241 placental mammals of the Zoonomia project.

_comment: A pre-filter, for size only. 3 rather than 5 for the same reason
as the main path: a variant can only reach a combined AC of 5 if
one callset has at least 3, so 3 cannot lose a variant the joint
callset kept. null keeps every score gnomAD publishes.
Both output tables are filtered to the variants the bundle
carries, by semi-join against the variant_masters parquet this
chromosome's joint DTP wrote.
This is a deliberate exception to ADR-003's rule that the two
data sources must not depend on each other. The rule exists so
the branches can run in any order; it is relaxed here because
the joint, exome and genome callsets are three files of one
gnomAD release, split across two DTPs only because they are
shaped differently.
The alternative was to sum AC_exomes + AC_genomes and keep what
reached 5. That is a proxy: the joint callset applies its own
QC, so a variant can clear the sum and still not be in the
bundle. Filtering against the file itself cannot be wrong.
Consequence: in a plan, a chromosome's joint source must precede
its VEP source. A missing variant_masters is a hard failure.
